newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says rate cut a low inflation reward.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says rate cut a low inflation reward.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) decision to cut official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 6.5 percent was a reward for low inflation and wage restraint and should be beneficial for jobs growth.
"It's a reward for low inflation and wage restraint," Howard told reporters.

Howard said the rate cut would help job creation and boost the economy, adding he expected it to flow through to home lower loan rates. "This cut in official rates will mean a flow through to housing rates and a further cut there," Howard said.

Asked what impact the move would have on jobs growth, he said: "It has to be beneficial, because lower rates means more investment, more risk taking -- therefore more potential for job generation. How much, I can't quantify."
Howard said lower interest rates would encourage investment and boost the economy.
"It's a boost. It will encourage people to take more risks to invest, to have a go and all of that helps," he said.
Howard said Australia's low inflation and wage moderation painted a bright picture for the economy.
